Subject: Pilot launch traffic & temporary quota bump request

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to get the pilot live. We’re targeting a limited pilot starting Nov 30 for two weeks. Early traffic profile (best estimate):

- Peak concurrent requests: ~220 RPS
- Peak sustained TPS during business hours: ~180 TPS for 2–3 hour windows
- Average latency tolerance: <= 600ms p95
- Major traffic spikes expected during 11:30–13:30 PT (user growth + scheduled batch jobs)

Attached is the launch plan and a short traffic forecast (pangea_launch_plan_v2.pdf). Can Redwood temporarily increase our quota/rate limits on the Hosted API for the pilot window? Ideally we’d like:

1) A burst quota to support up to 400 RPS for short windows (30–45 minutes)
2) A sustained per-second quota to 200 TPS for the pilot period
3) A contact for rapid support if we hit throttles during the first 72 hours

If you need any adjustments to the numbers or a brief call to align, happy to jump on 30–60 minute sync this week.

Thanks,
Sara

Markus — quick read through the plan. A few notes from capacity modelling:

- Hosted can handle a temporary uplift without Dedicated, but we need to coordinate routing and soft limits. Based on their numbers, recommend the following temporary config (pilot window Nov 30 — Dec 14):
  - Per-customer burst allowance: 400 RPS for 45-minute windows, throttled to 250 RPS for the rest of the hour (to protect cluster stability)
  - Sustained per-second quota: baseline 200 TPS with an automated cooldown rule if cluster-wide CPU > 75% for 10m
  - Token budgeting: assume average 35 tokens/request — this impacts cost and capacity, flagging to Finance for cost estimate

- Lead time: we can push the config by Nov 28 if Ops signs off today. Pre-warming: recommend warming heatmaps on Nov 29 for top 10 endpoints; I’ll provide a script.

- Risks: KV cache misses during sudden bursts may increase p95 by ~120–200ms for cold sessions. Pre-warm and a short-term increased batch size could help.

I’ll draft the exact rule change and the rollback policy — can own the implementation if Marcus can coordinate the pre-warm steps.

—Neha

Thanks — this makes sense. From CS/sales perspective:

- Pangea is high priority for Q4 proof points; they asked for as-close-to-zero friction. I recommend staged approach:
  - Stage 0 (Nov 29): pre-warm + confirmation of monitoring hooks and on-call coverage
  - Stage 1 (Nov 30 launch): soft bump to 250 RPS with auto-escalation to 400 RPS by request if metrics look healthy (we should gate escalation on CPU and error rate)
  - Stage 2 (Dec 2): if stable, move to sustained 200 TPS baseline for remainder of pilot

- SLA/credits: they asked about support contact. We can offer a dedicated on-call rotation for the launch window (Marcus to confirm availability). For credits, keep language conservative — offer operational support rather than blanket credits unless we have a major outage.

- Communication: we should send Pangea a short runbook (how we’ll throttle, who to contact, expected escalation steps) and a single Slack channel for launch ops. I can draft the runbook and own the Slack channel.
